slides.title: 5 Italian words English forgot to invent
slides.sub: Your vocabulary is about to get an upgrade.

slides.meaning: The sleepiness that hits after a big meal. A medical condition. (Not officially.)
slides.ex_it: Dopo le lasagne della nonna, abbiocco totale.
slides.ex_en: After nonna's lasagna: total food coma.

slides.meaning: The wet ring a cold glass leaves on the table. Yes, we named it.
slides.ex_en: Use a coaster — no glass rings!

slides.meaning: The lady who feeds every stray cat in the neighbourhood. Every street has one.
slides.ex_it: La gattara del quartiere ha quattordici gatti.
slides.ex_en: The neighbourhood cat lady has fourteen cats.

slides.meaning: The fine art of not caring. Some Italians hold a master's degree in it.
An aperitivo so generous it becomes dinner. Pure strategy.

slides.title: Which one do you need in your life?
slides.text: Comment yours — and follow for more Italian you won't find in a dictionary.

caption:
5 Italian words English forgot to invent 🇮🇹

Abbiocco · Culaccino · Gattara · Menefreghismo · Apericena

One language has a word for the ring your glass leaves on the table. The other doesn't. We're not saying which one is superior. (We are.)

Which one will you steal? 👇
